messages:
maya: Quick sync — I'm opening a small docs PR to add a short section on how we normalize benchmark numbers in model cards across GPUs/regions. Draft here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1456 :wave:

ben: Nice. Are we clarifying p50 vs p95, and per-token vs per-sequence? Those confuse customers a lot.

maya: Yes. Plan is: define measurement (seq len, batch), list hardware, show raw numbers + normalized throughput per v100/a100/h100 equivalence, and include a short note about warmup + KV cache.

kenji: Please call out quantized variants explicitly. For int8/4 we should show delta vs fp16 and note any changed seq ceilings.

maya: Good call. I'll add a small table and a short snippet showing the exact bench command we used.

(taylor): +1 on table. Also add a short paragraph about cross-region noise — e.g., 5-10% variance due to network+cpu scheduling if you measure over the public hosted endpoints.

ben: For normalization math, can we use a simple baseline conversion function? e.g. throughput_norm = raw_throughput * (baseline_flops / measured_flops). That might be oversimplified but gives customers an idea.

maya: I'll add a note that it's heuristic and link to the perf-harness README.

kenji: Example bench command would help. Suggest something like:
```
# perf harness (example)
python perf_harness.py \n  --model orion-xl \n  --seq_len 2048 \n  --batch 1 \n  --iters 300 \n  --device a100 \n  --quant none \n  --collect p50,p95,throughput
```

taylor: Can you include the raw sample output too? e.g. p50=18ms, p95=32ms, tokens/s=1200 so people can map numbers.

maya: Yup. I'll paste a small example block in the PR. Also adding a tiny FAQ bullet: "How do we compare across GPUs?" with recommended caveats.

ben: Who should review? I can do a tech pass for the math. Kenji for quant notes. Docs editorial review from Taylor.

maya: Thanks — assigning reviewers in PR. @docs-bot can we add a short checklist comment when PR is opened?

docs-bot: I will post the PR checklist once the PR is opened. (automated)

kenji: One more thought: call out sequence-length ceilings — e.g., some variants hit memory limits at 4096 and should be labeled. Don't forget to link model-catalog limit fields.

maya: Good — linking to the model-catalog limits page and adding anchor links. Also doing a quick sweep to ensure we don't duplicate existing model-card texts.

ben: Link-fix note: the current model-catalog page has an outdated link to the perf-harness README. If you hit it, replace with https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness#readme

maya: I'll update that in the PR too. Expect the draft by EOD. If anyone wants to edit directly, I left a short TODO in the PR description for the conversion math and the sample table.

(taylor): Great. If you can, add a one-line callout in the top of the model card template so writers remember to include the baseline machine info.

maya: Added to the PR TODOs. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ben: merging procedure question — should we wait for perf infra to re-run the canonical numbers after edits?

kenji: Ideally yes, but we can merge the docs change and tag a follow-up perf-run task (GH issue) if timeline is tight. Add a CHANGENOTES entry.

maya: Will do. Last_message_ts=3420001430
